title: Operad-natural adjunction on infinity operadic algebras
statement:
Use the universes and presentably monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads and their algebra categories as defined in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal W$ be a colimit-preserving strong monoidal functor between presentably monoidal infinity categories, and let $f\dashv g$ have unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. The right adjoint has its adjoint lax monoidal structure. For every small ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operad $\mathcal O$, postcomposition induces functors $f_{\mathcal O}:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal W)$ and $g_{\mathcal O}$ in the reverse direction, and a natural equivalence of mapping-space bifunctors
$$\operatorname{Map}(f_{\mathcal O}A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A,g_{\mathcal O}B).$$
Its two directions send $k$ to $g_{\mathcal O}(k)\eta_A$ and $h$ to $\varepsilon_B f_{\mathcal O}(h)$; the unit and counit are algebra transformations whose components on every color are $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$. For every map $u:\mathcal O'\to\mathcal O$ of small ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads, these equivalences commute coherently with restriction $u^*$, including their units, counits and triangle homotopies. Thus these are adjunctions natural in the operad, not merely bijections of homotopy classes.

source.place: Proposition A.5.11 and its proof (restriction-natural adjunction for ordinary nonsymmetric operadic algebras). Read online; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Write $F:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\mathcal W^\otimes$ for the strong monoidal functor presenting $f$. By [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], its fibers over $[n]$ identify with $f^n:\mathcal V^n\to\mathcal W^n$. The product of the given mapping-space equivalences is
$$\prod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal W}(f v_i,w_i)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v_i,g w_i).$$
Thus $f^n\dashv g^n$, with coordinatewise units and counits. This includes $n=0$: both fibers and both mapping spaces are terminal. All categories fit in a common enlarged universe. Strongness says exactly that $F$ preserves cocartesian arrows over the base.

source.place: Corollary 7.3.2.7, proof, Segal product calculation, applied to the nonsymmetric simplex model

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-relative-right-adjoint] to $F$ over $S=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, using the fiber adjunctions of Step 1 and the cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Obtain $G:\mathcal W^\otimes\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $S$ with a relative adjunction $F\dashv G$. Denote its unit and counit by $\eta^\otimes,\varepsilon^\otimes$. Normalize its fiber adjunctions by the supplied equivalences of adjunction data, so that over $[1]$ they are the specified $f\dashv g$, and over $[n]$ their coordinatewise products. In particular their components lie over identity arrows of $S$.

We check that $G$ is lax monoidal by computing its effect on inert arrows. For an inert $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, let $P_\alpha$ select the corresponding consecutive coordinates. In both monoidal fibrations its cocartesian transport is $P_\alpha$. For a cocartesian lift $e:w\to P_\alpha w$ in $\mathcal W^\otimes$, factor $G(e)$ through a cocartesian lift in $\mathcal V^\otimes$ as a vertical map
$$v:P_\alpha g^n w\longrightarrow g^m P_\alpha w.$$
The factorization and its uniqueness as a mapping-space equivalence follow by taking the fiber over $\alpha$ in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Naturality of $\varepsilon^\otimes$ identifies the adjunct of $v$ with $P_\alpha\varepsilon_w$. Since the fiber counit is coordinatewise, this is the counit of $f^m\dashv g^m$ at $P_\alpha w$. The counit calculation identifies $v$ with the canonical coordinate equivalence $P_\alpha g^n w\simeq g^mP_\alpha w$. Hence $v$ is an equivalence, so the same mapping-space criterion makes $G(e)$ cocartesian. For $m=0$ this is the identity in the terminal fiber. Thus $G$ preserves all inert arrows. Its comparison on an active $[r]\to[1]$ is the adjunct of
$$ f(\bigotimes_i g w_i)\simeq\bigotimes_i f g w_i\xrightarrow{\bigotimes_i\varepsilon_{w_i}}\bigotimes_i w_i.$$
For $r=0$ the map is $f(\mathbf1_{\mathcal V})\simeq\mathbf1_{\mathcal W}$. This identifies its lax structure with the adjoint lax monoidal structure, including the nullary operation. The substitution coherences belong to the already coherent functor $G$ and its counit; no separate aritywise choices are made.

source.place: Corollary 7.3.2.7, proof, inert-preservation calculation; Remark 7.3.2.9, mate comparison, in the nonsymmetric model

proof.text: For a small ordinary nonsymmetric operad $\mathcal O$, its algebra category is the category of inert-preserving functors over $S$, as in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Composition with $F$ and $G$ preserves this condition, so defines $f_{\mathcal O}$ and $g_{\mathcal O}$. Whiskering $\eta^\otimes$ by $A$ and $\varepsilon^\otimes$ by $B$ gives transformations $A\to GFA$ and $FGB\to B$ over $S$. Their endpoints are inert-preserving functors, and whiskering gives coherent transformations of such functors, so these are algebra transformations. Their color components are exactly $\eta_{A(c)}$ and $\varepsilon_{B(c)}$.

source.place: Proposition A.5.11, adjunction conclusion; Lemma A.5.12, proof, restriction to the full algebra subcategories

proof.text:
Apply the coherent-diagram clause of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $T=F$, $\mathcal D_0=\mathcal W^\otimes$, and the universal counit supplied by [lem-coef-cocartesian-relative-right-adjoint], with diagram shape $K=\mathcal O$. It gives a natural equivalence on the functor-category mapping spaces, with inverse $k\mapsto G(k)(\eta^\otimes A)$. Both formulas lie over the same base transformation because $F,G,\eta^\otimes,\varepsilon^\otimes$ are over $S$. Restrict to transformations over the identity of the fixed map $\mathcal O\to S$, and then to the inert-preserving functors and their coherent transformations that define the algebra categories. The formulas are
$$\Phi(k)=G(k)\eta_A,\qquad\Psi(h)=\varepsilon_BF(h).$$
The inverse homotopies can also be seen directly in these subcategories:
$$\Psi\Phi(k)\simeq k\,\varepsilon_{FA}F\eta_A\simeq k,\qquad
\Phi\Psi(h)\simeq G\varepsilon_B\,\eta_{GB}h\simeq h.$$
The first homotopies are naturality of counit and unit, and the second are their relative triangle homotopies, all whiskered by the same diagrams. These homotopies stay over the identity of the base, so the restriction is an equivalence of entire mapping spaces. This supplies the stated bifunctor equivalence and the algebra triangle homotopies.

source.place: Proposition A.5.11, mapping-space adjunction, with its explicit postcomposition realization as in the proof of Lemma A.5.12

proof.text:
Let $u:\mathcal O'\to\mathcal O$ preserve inert arrows. Restriction is precomposition. For every algebra map $k$ and $h$, associativity of composition gives, coherently,
$$u^*(G(k)\eta_A)=G(u^*k)\eta_{u^*A},\qquad
u^*(\varepsilon_BF(h))=\varepsilon_{u^*B}F(u^*h).$$
Both identities are identities of whiskered coherent transformations, so also hold on all higher simplices. The precomposition compatibility in [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] supplies the same compatibility for the mapping-space equivalence. Units and counits restrict by their definition in Step 4, and the inverse homotopies in Step 5 restrict by the same whiskering. For an identity, a composite of operad maps, or a higher simplex of such maps, these are restrictions of the same $F,G,\eta^\otimes,\varepsilon^\otimes$ and triangle homotopies. Thus the compatibility includes all composition coherences in the operad variable.

source.place: Proposition A.5.11, proof, naturality in the operad; explicit precomposition calculation

The item statement is unchanged; it is no weaker than GH A.5.11 (restricted to ordinary operads) and keeps all its hypotheses. The new node lem-coef-cocartesian-relative-right-adjoint (fiberwise right adjoints of a cocartesian-preserving functor assemble to a right adjoint relative to the base; the dual of HA 7.3.2.6, plus 7.3.2.5 for base change) is true. I proved it directly: Map^α(Fx,y) ≃ Map_{D_t}(α_!F x,y) ≃ Map_{D_t}(F α_!x,y) ≃ Map(α_!x,R_t y) ≃ Map^α(x,R y). I tested it on S a point, S empty, F the identity, and the Set/Ab one-arrow case, where R does not preserve cocartesian edges, as the statement allows. It meets B1–B7 and has three-kind Mathlib searches. rg over the DAG and the main-20261015 blueprint finds no duplicate. It is not a restated clause of the item: it mentions no operads or algebras. Steps: 1 (Segal fibers, f^n ⊣ g^n, n=0 is the point) is elementary. 2 supplies every hypothesis of the new node. 3 is the inert-preservation argument in the style of HA 7.3.2.7: it uses the cocartesian mapping criterion and the counit adjunct P_α ε, and the mate of ⊗ε gives the adjoint lax structure, including the unit. 4 is whiskering into full algebra subcategories. 5 applies the parametric universal-arrow node with K = O^⊗ and restricts to fibers over the identity; the triangle homotopies are checked. 6 is strict compatibility of precomposition with postcomposition and whiskering. proof_deps equals the union of uses, there is no cycle, and every cited statement node is in the unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed. The parent lem-coef-enrichment-change-adjunction gets exactly the clauses it uses.
